newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN MOVES INTO EIGHTH PLACE ON ALL-TIME SCORING LIST.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN MOVES INTO EIGHTH PLACE ON ALL-TIME SCORING LIST.

text.p: Scottie Pippen scored 29 points and Michael Jordan had 23 to take eighth place on the all-time scoring list as the Chicago Bulls beat the Minnesota Timberwolves, 112-102 on Wednesday.
Pippen sparked the key burst, which saw the Bulls turn a 75-74 deficit into a 12-point lead with 9:24 to play.

Jordan's 25,620 points moved him past long-time Denver Nugget Alex English. Jordan is now on the heels of the NBA's active scoring leader, San Antonio's Dominique Wilkins, who led Jordan by 279 points entering play tonight.
The Bulls, who improved to 16-0 all-time against the Timberwolves, have won eight straight games and own the league's best record at 33-4.

In Charlotte, Glen Rice scored 35 points and Vlade Divac added 25 points, 12 rebounds and eight assists as the Charlotte Hornets overcame an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit en route to a 116-104 victory over the New Jersey Nets.
Anthony Mason had 20 points, 17 rebounds and eight assists. Muggsy Bogues had 13 points and nine assists and Dell Curry added 13 points for the Hornets.
Ex-Hornet Kendall Gill followed up a career-high 41 points against Orlando with 30 points for the Nets.
In Vancouver, Grant Hill scored 12 of his 31 points in the first quarter and fell one assist shy of a triple-double as the Detroit Pistons coasted to a 103-79 rout of the Vancouver Grizzlies.
Lindsey Hunter added 16 points, Terry Mills had 14, including four three-pointers, and Grant Long scored 12 for Detroit, which has won seven of its last nine games.
"Their defence had something to do with our poor shooting," Vancouver coach Brian Winters said. "When you dig such a big hole against a good team, it's hard to come back."
In Dallas, Penny Hardaway had 26 points, seven rebounds and six assists as the Orlando Magic held the Dallas Mavericks to a franchise-low point total in a 78-66 victory.
Horace Grant had 14 points and nine rebounds and Gerald Wilkins added 11 points.
Derek Harper and Jim Jackson each scored 12 points for Dallas.

In Los Angeles, Reggie Miller scored 25 points and became the second player in NBA history to make 1,300 three-pointers as the Indiana Pacers defeated the Los Angeles Clippers for the eighth straight time, 108-93.
Miller's 1,300th career three-pointer gave the Pacers the lead for good, 44-43, with 5:12 left in the second quarter. He shot 4-for-8 from three-point range.
In Philadelphia, Latrell Sprewell scored 16 of his 38 points in the first quarter as the Golden State Warriors held off the reeling Philadelphia 76ers, 128-111.

Joe Smith added 26 points for the Warriors, who won for just the second time in six games. Golden State jumped to a 73-52 halftime lead on the strength of 68 percent shooting (32-of-47) from the floor.
Clarence Weatherspoon scored 34 points and Jerry Stackhouse added 23 for Philadelphia, which has lost 10 straight games and 20 of its last 21.
In Seattle, Sam Perkins tied an NBA single-game record by making eight three-pointers without a miss and the Seattle SuperSonics used a league-record 27 steals to rout the Toronto Raptors, 122-78.
Perkins' shooting matched the performance set by Utah's Jeff Hornacek in 1994, against Seattle.
In winning their sixth consecutive game, the SuperSonics broke the NBA-mark of 25 steals accomplished twice by the Golden State Warriors.
Perkins scored 26 points and Shawn Kemp had 25 points for Seattle.

In San Antonio, Allan Houston scored 13 of his 20 points in the third quarter and Patrick Ewing added 18 points and 11 rebounds as the New York Knicks cruised to their fifth victory in six games, 94-77 over the floundering San Antonio Spurs.
New York rebounded from a 106-86 blowout Tuesday in Houston and moved a half-game ahead of the Miami Heat for the lead in the Atlantic Division.
Vernon Maxwell scored 22 points and Sean Elliott added 14 for the Spurs.
